chunks: Al-Ṣaffār, from Al-Sindī ibn Al-Rabīʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from his father, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The one upon whom stoning is obligatory is stoned from behind, and is not stoned from his face, because stoning and striking are not directed at the face; rather, they are carried out upon the body, upon all of the limbs.

key_terms.اَلرَّجْمُ: stoning as a prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.اَلضَّرْبَ: striking or hitting in the context of punishment
key_terms.اَلْأَعْضَاءِ: the limbs or bodily parts generally
key_terms.اَلْجَسَدِ: the body, which is the place where the punishment is applied
key_terms.مِنْ وَرَائِهِ: from behind, indicating the manner of application
key_terms.وَجْهِهِ: his face, which is not to be targeted

ai.seo_question: How is rajm to be carried out according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the manner in which rajm is to be carried out. It specifies that the face is not to be targeted, and that the punishment is directed toward the body and the rest of the limbs.
